Distribution Function and Its Derivatives from the Compiled Kernels

Source: R/cdf_compiled.R
compiled_cdf.Rd

Provides the method bodies for distrib_cdf(), distrib_grad_cdf() and distrib_hess_cdf() that read the compiled distribution functions of the package's scalar registry, for the families whose distribution function has no closed derivative in a shape parameter: the gamma (both parametrizations), the chi-squared, the two generalized gammas, the two betas, the two von Mises, the two Student t, the two pseudo-Huber and the skew t.

Usage

compiled_cdf(distrib, q, theta, lower.tail = TRUE, log.p = FALSE, ...)

compiled_log_cdf(distrib, a, out, lower.tail)

log_tail_integral(distrib, q, th, lower.tail)

compiled_grad_cdf(distrib, q, theta, lower.tail = TRUE, log = TRUE, ...)

compiled_hess_cdf(distrib, q, theta, lower.tail = TRUE, log = TRUE, ...)

compiled_cdf_args(distrib, q, theta)

Arguments

distrib

A distribution object of one of the families above.

q

A numeric vector of quantiles.

theta

A named list of parameter values.

lower.tail

A single logical; TRUE selects the lower tail and FALSE the upper tail.

...

Unused.

a

The value of compiled_cdf_args().

out

The probabilities of the requested tail, from the compiled kernel.

th

A named list of scalar parameter values.

log, log.p

A single logical; if TRUE, derivatives of (or values of) the log probability are returned.

Value

For compiled_cdf(), a numeric vector; for the two derivative bodies, a named list of numeric vectors as distrib_grad_cdf() and distrib_hess_cdf() return.

compiled_far_tail() returns the logical vector of the quantiles whose requested tail is below \(e^{-5}\), inside the support.

compiled_log_cdf() returns the logarithm of out, formed as \(\log(1 - P_{\mathrm{other}})\) through log1p() where out is above one half, and as \(\ell(q) + \log\int_{\mathrm{tail}} e^{\ell(y) - \ell(q)}\,dy\) where out is below \(e^{-5}\); there quad_log_tail_prob() computes the integral on the scale \(1/|\partial_y \ell(q)|\).

log_tail_integral() returns the logarithm of the probability of the tail beyond q, \(\ell(q) + \log\int_0^\infty e^{\ell(q \mp u) - \ell(q)}\,du\), by stats::integrate() on a scale adjusted until one step changes \(\ell\) by between 1/2 and 50, and \(\ell(q) - \log|\ell'(q)|\) where such a step cannot be resolved.

compiled_cdf_args() returns the class name, the recycled quantiles and the parameter matrix that the kernels read.

Details

A derivative in a shape parameter is the integral of the density's own derivative, $$\partial_k F(q) = \int_{-\infty}^{q} f\, s_k \, dy, \qquad \partial_{kl} F(q) = \int_{-\infty}^{q} f\,(\ell_{kl} + s_k s_l)\, dy,$$ with \(s\) and \(\ell\) the score and the Hessian of the log-density. The integral is taken by a fixed rule (tanh-sinh panels doubling away from the family's center, an exp-sinh tail beyond), in \(\log y\) on \((0, \infty)\) and in \(\mathrm{logit}(y)\) on \((0, 1)\), so that a density that behaves like \(y^{k-1}\) at an end of its support is integrated as an exponential tail; in \(\log y\) the panels are at most one unit wide, and they restart at the scale \(\theta\) where the density's fast decay begins when that point lies more than one unit above the center. For a small \(k\) part of the mass lies below the smallest representable double, so on \((0, \infty)\) the part below \(y_0 = \min(q, 10^{-290})\) is integrated in closed form wherever it holds at least \(10^{-17}\) of \(F(q)\): there the log-density and its parameter derivatives are linear in \(L = \log y\), so they are read at \(10^{-290}\) and 15 units of \(L\) below it and extended to \(L_0 = \log y_0\), and \(\int_{-\infty}^{L_0} e^{c + k u} g(u)\, du = f(y_0)\, y_0 \sum_j (-1)^j g^{(j)}(L_0)/k^{j+1}\) (compiled_cdf_head() at orders three and four). When the part of the support above \(q\) holds less mass than the part below, the integral runs over the upper part with the opposite sign, so that a derivative that is small beside one is not a sum of terms of order one; the mass is the family's closed distribution function where it has one, and the integral of the density otherwise. The two beta families always integrate the lower part when their second shape is below one. For the families that are location-scale in \((\mu, \sigma)\) only the shape parameters are integrated: with \(z = (q - \mu)/\sigma\) the location and scale components are \(-f\), \(-z f\) and, at second order, \(-f s_\mu\), \(f(-z^2 s_\mu + 2z/\sigma)\) and \(f(-z s_\mu + 1/\sigma)\), and the mixed components with a shape \(k\) are \(-f s_k\) and \(-z f s_k\), all at \(q\). The distribution function itself is pt(), pgamma(), pchisq() or pbeta() where the family has one, and the same integral of the density otherwise; with log.p = TRUE its logarithm is formed by compiled_log_cdf(), so that it stays finite in either tail. The lower-tail derivatives are converted to the requested tail and log scale, as for every family.
